events.region: Livingston, LA; St. Helena, LA; Tangipahoa, LA
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northeastern Livingston Parish in southeastern Louisiana...
Southeastern St. Helena Parish in southeastern Louisiana...
Southern Tangipahoa Parish in southeastern Louisiana...

* WHEN...Until 215 PM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1117 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Hammond, Ponchatoula, Livingston, Independence, Albany,
Springfield, Montpelier, Natalbany, Robert, Killian and Tickfaw.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.region: North Mobile Bay; South Mobile Bay; Mississippi Sound; Coastal waters from Pensacola FL to Pascagoula MS out 20 NM
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 1113 AM CDT...A strong thunderstorm was located over Fort Gaines,
or near Sand Island Lighthouse...moving north at 15 knots.

Locations impacted include...
Central Dauphin Island, East Fowl River Bridge, Sand Island
Lighthouse, Dauphin Island Bridge, Fort Gaines, Fort Morgan, Western
Dauphin Island, Heron Bay, Alabama Port, and Portersville Bay.

The primary threats from this storm are wind gusts up to 30 knots...
locally higher waves...and heavy downpours. Boaters should consider
seeking safe harbor until this storm has passed.

Weather conditions support the development of waterspouts.
Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally hazardous
waves and seas. If a waterspout is sighted...seek safe harbor
immediately.

events.region: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; Southeast; Eastern Interior; North Central; Central Interior; Ponce and Vicinity; Northwest; Western Interior; Mayaguez and Vicinity; Southwest
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...This level of heat can affect anyone without effective
cooling and/or adequate hydration.

* WHERE...A portion of Puerto Rico.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM AST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Heat-related illnesses increase significantly during
periods of very high heat indices or high temperatures. This
extreme heat event poses a severe threat to anyone with inadequate
cooling or hydration. These extreme impacts will be most pronounced
across coastal sections, lowlands, interior valleys, and urban
areas.

events.region: Culebra; Vieques; St.Thomas...St. John.. and Adjacent Islands; St Croix
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to
heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration.

* WHERE...In Puerto Rico, Culebra and Vieques. In Virgin Islands, St
Croix and St. Thomas, St. John, and Adjacent Islands.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM AST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...High temperatures or elevated heat indices can worsen
symptoms in people with chronic conditions. They can also increase
the risk of heat-related illness among individuals sensitive to
heat with inadequate cooling or hydration. These risks are highest
across coastal areas, lowlands, interior valleys, and urban zones.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWLIX

The National Weather Service in New Orleans has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Hancock County in southern Mississippi...
Southwestern Harrison County in southern Mississippi...

* Until 1245 PM CDT.

* At 1046 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 3 and 6 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Long Beach, Bay St. Louis, Waveland, Pass Christian, Diamondhead,
Shoreline Park and Kiln.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Southwestern Cochise County in southeastern Arizona,
specifically Hereford Road between milepost 8 and 9.

* WHEN...Until 230 PM MST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water is spilling onto Hereford Rd near the one lane bridge that
goes over the San Pedro River.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 834 AM MST, local law enforcement reported runoff from earlier
heavy rain in the advisory area. This is causing small stream
flooding. Overflowing poor drainage areas have already caused
minor flooding in the advisory area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Hereford Road between milepost 8 and 9.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
